title: Icon model save override drops positional save arguments
reasoning: Django model save overrides must accept positional arguments as well as keyword arguments because callers and Django internals can legally call save(False, False, using, update_fields). This override only accepts **kwargs, so any valid positional save call raises TypeError before reaching Django's Model.save. The included icon tests only exercise Icon.objects.create and never call save with positional arguments, so they do not establish compatibility with the base Model.save API.
reproduction: Call icon.save(False, False, None, ['title']) on an existing Icon instance; Python raises TypeError because Icon.save accepts no positional arguments.
recommendation: Change the override to def save(self, *args, **kwargs): and pass *args through to super().save(*args, **kwargs) in every super save call where appropriate. Keep the update_fields-only internal cache saves as keyword calls.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: icons/tests.py creates Icons through objects.create and checks basic fields, but it never exercises direct save calls with positional arguments or compatibility with Django's documented Model.save signature.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a model test that updates an Icon and calls save(False, False, None, ['title']) or another positional-argument save form, asserting it does not raise and persists the update.
minimumFixScope: icons/models.py Icon.save signature and the primary super().save call.
